key_insight: VLMs can evaluate medical image quality, but their scores are highly sensitive to image corruption and even non-image metadata.
clinical_relevance: This matters because unreliable image-quality judgments could affect whether scans are trusted for downstream clinical decisions, especially when privacy-preserving degradation or contextual bias is present.
method: Benchmarked 16 vision-language models zero-shot on MediMeta-C
Tested 7 corruption types across 5 severity levels
Checked effects of image degradation, embedding shifts, and textual metadata
evidence_signal: Across seven modalities, pixelation caused the largest average score drop (-20.58%), while brightness had minimal impact (-0.81%); metadata also shifted scores substantially.
watch_item: Do not assume VLM-based quality assessment is objective or privacy-neutral, since both corruption and contextual attributes can meaningfully bias outputs.
paper_title: Assessing VLM Reliability for Medical Image Quality Evaluation Under Corruption and Bias
